current_workflow.step: A settlements or volume analyst finds an unexplained volume at a meter (UA4 balance, measured flow with no deal, or a short delivery), often months after the gas flowed.
The analyst researches by hand across OSS, CPR and MIPs measurement statements to see whether a deal or measurement exists for the meter and month.
The analyst emails the logistics desk (mostly Daren Farmer) or the scheduler to ask whether a deal is missing, what a nomination was for, or how a short day should be handled.
Feed failures between POPS and Sitara come to light only when someone reviews imbalance numbers. The zero volumes then have to be overridden by hand so the P&L is right.
Open variances pile up in periodic lists (the interdesk/interconnect report, the feedback error report), each with a named owner working it through emails and calls.

Once a cause is agreed, staff zero confirmed noms, change the allocation method, reallocate the meter in POPS, and extend or create deals in Sitara. These steps are done by hand and handed off by phone.
People who opened an item but got no answer send follow-ups, or escalate when a counterparty calls asking to be paid.

implementation_steps: Inventory the extract points: which POPS, Sitara and measurement tables or reports can be read daily, and how OSS/CPR history can be reached. Confirm read-only access with each system owner.
Build the meter/day join keyed on meter number, contract and deal (Sitara ticket and track id), and test it against the known cases in the evidence (meters 1441, 986782, 984132, Valero Texoma #71).
Write the first three rules (flow with no valid deal, out-of-term confirmation, zero POPS-to-Sitara feed). Set tolerances with volume management, then backtest on one closed month.
Build the meter-to-owner routing table with the logistics desk, schedulers and volume management. Add the disposition field and exception list.
Run in shadow mode for one month next to the existing interdesk/interconnect report and feedback error report. Compare what each catches and tune false positives.
Add the remaining rules (delivery noms on receipt meters, confirmed vs actual mismatch, UA4 growth) and the aging digest.
Go live: analysts log new variance questions as dispositions on exception items instead of emailing the desk. Review open-item aging weekly.
risks: The evidence does not show whether POPS, Sitara, OSS, CPR or MIPs offer usable extracts or interfaces. Integration could be harder than estimated, so confirm access before committing.
Measurement is often restated or arrives late (outside-measured meters, prior-period adjustments). The job should re-run prior months and label items as provisional until measurement is final.
Tolerances set too tight would flood analysts with noise and they would go back to email. Start with high-value rules, backtest, and tune during shadow mode.
Meter numbering and facility changes (e.g. meter 986892 replaced by 980439) can break the join. Maintain a meter-change mapping fed by the facility change process.

The measured benefit is small ($68/month, $816/year at $85/hour), because only about 4 messages a month are counted. The P&L exposure from undetected UA4 and feed failures is not priced here and is the stronger case, so it should be validated separately.
If owners keep resolving items by phone and email, dispositions go unrecorded and the aging digest misleads. Make the disposition entry part of closing an item.

solution.approach: A daily variance job pulls, for every meter and gas day, the measured volume (MIPs measurement), the confirmed noms and allocations in POPS, and the deals and volumes in Sitara (with OSS/CPR for older production months). It applies a fixed set of rules: flow with no valid deal on that day, a confirmation on a date outside the deal's term, zero volumes fed from POPS back to Sitara where flow exists, delivery noms on receipt meters, confirmed volume not matching allocated actuals beyond a tolerance, and a UA4 balance growing at a meter. Each exception goes on one shared list with the meter, month, volumes on each side, the prior month for context and the rule that fired. It is routed by rule to an owner: logistics desk for missing or invalid deals, scheduler for nomination issues, volume management for allocation and feed problems. Owners record a disposition on the item instead of starting an email thread. Items left open past an age threshold are flagged on a daily digest, so follow-ups and escalations are no longer needed.
components: Daily meter variance comparison job (measurement vs POPS vs Sitara)
Rule set with tolerances (no-deal flow, out-of-term confirmation, zero feed, delivery nom on receipt meter, confirmed vs actual mismatch, UA4 growth)
Exception list with owner routing and a disposition field (fix deal, reallocate, accept variance, counterparty dispute)
Feed-health check that alerts on zero POPS-to-Sitara volumes
Aging digest replacing manual follow-up emails
inputs: Measured meter volumes by gas day (MIPs measurement statements)
POPS confirmed nominations, allocation method and allocated volumes per meter and contract
Sitara deal tickets: term dates, meter, volumes fed back from POPS
OSS and CPR deal records for prior production months
outputs: Daily exception list per meter and month, with volumes from each source, the prior month, and the rule that fired, for volume management and settlements analysts
Routed exception items for the logistics desk (missing or invalid deal), schedulers (nomination on wrong meter type, short delivery) and volume management (feed failure, allocation mismatch)
Same-day alert when POPS feeds zero volumes to Sitara for deals with measured flow
Aging digest of open exceptions, with disposition history, for the volume management lead
solution.trigger: Daily schedule after the POPS allocation run and the POPS-to-Sitara volume feed. A month-end run also covers the full production month.

stays_manual: Deciding which volume is correct when sources disagree (e.g. pipeline vs HPL Measurement custody transfer) is a commercial and contractual judgment for volume management.
Deciding whether to create, extend or change a deal, or arrange a buyback, stays with the logistics desk and traders.

Reallocations, zeroing confirmed noms and facility changes in POPS stay human-executed, because they ripple into Gas Control and settlements (the evidence shows a multi-party, phone-coordinated sequence).
Disputes and payment claims from counterparties, and questions needing Legal input, stay with people.
Choosing tolerances and approving which rules route to whom.
success_metric: Median days from a meter variance first appearing (flow, POPS or Sitara mismatch) to its disposition, together with the monthly count of variance-research emails to the logistics desk and the number of POPS-to-Sitara zero-feed days caught within 24 hours.
summary: Settlements, volume management and logistics staff find meter allocation exceptions one at a time: a meter with flow but no deal, POPS feeding zero volumes to Sitara, or a desk-to-desk volume variance. Each one becomes its own email thread to Daren Farmer's logistics desk and can wait days or weeks. A daily variance job would compare measured flow, POPS confirmed noms and allocations, and Sitara deals per meter, then route each exception with its supporting data to the right owner. Analysts would work one ranked exception list instead of researching and chasing each meter by email.
